questions.q: What happens if you run Insert on a CSV file you've already successfully loaded once before?
options: Data Loader detects the duplicate and skips those rows automatically
Every row creates a brand-new record, producing duplicates
The job fails outright with no records processed
Insert automatically switches to Update behavior
questions.explain: Insert never checks for an existing match — every row becomes a new record, so reloading the same file produces duplicates.

questions.q: What does Update match on, and what happens to a row with no value in that field?
options: It matches on Email, and the row is skipped quietly
It matches on record ID, and the row fails outright
It matches on Name, and the row is inserted as new instead
It matches on whatever field is listed first in the CSV
questions.explain: Update matches purely on the Salesforce record ID. A row missing that ID has nothing to match against and fails — there's no fallback to name or another field.

questions.q: Why is Upsert often the safer default for a recurring sync where you're not sure which rows already exist?
options: It runs faster than Insert or Update in every case
It can update a matching record or insert a new one, avoiding both false duplicates and hard failures
It doesn't require a CSV file, unlike the other two operations
It automatically fixes any formatting errors in the source file
questions.explain: Upsert checks its match field first — updating when it finds a hit, inserting when it doesn't — so it avoids the duplicate risk of guessing Insert and the hard failure of Update on an unmatched row.

questions.q: By default, what happens when a CSV cell is left blank during an Update or Upsert job?
options: The existing value in that field is overwritten with null
The entire row is rejected
The field is skipped, leaving the existing value untouched
Data Loader asks the user to fill in a value before continuing
questions.explain: By default, a blank cell is simply skipped and the existing value stays as it was. Checking Insert null values changes this so a blank cell instead clears the field.

questions.q: Why does checking "Insert null values" matter for a job built from an incomplete export?
options: It has no practical effect on real data
It only changes behavior for the Insert operation, not Update or Upsert
With it off, a missing column's existing data is protected; with it on, that data gets wiped to null
It only applies when using the Import Wizard, not Data Loader
questions.explain: If an export accidentally drops a column, the default (off) behavior leaves existing values alone. With Insert null values on, that same gap would overwrite existing data with null instead.
